concepts.title: Newton's First Law of Motion
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, an object remains in its state of rest or uniform linear motion unless an external unbalanced force acts upon it.
concepts.key_idea: Objects have inertia, resisting changes to their state of motion.
question_patterns: explain why a passenger jerks forward when a bus stops
what happens to an object if the net external force is zero
define the law of inertia
identify the state of motion when forces are balanced

solution_steps.explain: List all forces acting on the body from the environment.
Sum the force vectors to check if they cancel out.

concepts.title: Linear Momentum
concepts.definition: The vector quantity representing the product of an object's mass and its instantaneous velocity.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Momentum quantifies the 'amount of motion' and varies with both mass and speed.
question_patterns: calculate the momentum of a body
find the product of mass and velocity
what is the momentum of a mass m moving at speed v
how much momentum does a vehicle have

solution_steps.explain: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.

concepts.title: Newton's Second Law of Motion
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the net force acting on a body equals the result of multiplying its mass and the acceleration produced.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Force is indeed the rate of change of momentum over time.
question_patterns: calculate the force required to accelerate a mass
find the acceleration of a body under a given force
what is the net force acting on the object
determine the mass if force and acceleration are known

solution_steps.explain: Force is calculated as mass times acceleration.

concepts.title: Impulse
concepts.definition: The product of a large force and the short time interval during which it acts, resulting in a change in momentum.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Impulse measures the total change in momentum brought about by a force.
question_patterns: calculate the impulse imparted to a ball
find the change in momentum
what is the product of force and time
determine the impulse from mass and velocity change

solution_steps.explain: Find the difference between final and initial velocity.
Impulse equals the change in momentum.

concepts.title: Newton's Third Law of Motion
concepts.definition: In brief, Whenever two bodies interact, the force applied by the first on the second is equal in both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both magnitude and opposite in direction to the force applied by the second on the first.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Forces always exist in pairs acting on different bodies.
question_patterns: state the law of action and reaction
identify the reaction force to a given action
why do action and reaction forces not cancel each other
explain how a swimmer pushes the water

solution_steps.explain: Determine the two objects exerting forces on each other.
Force on A by B is equal and opposite to force on B by A.

concepts.title: Law of Conservation of Momentum
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the total linear momentum of an isolated system remains constant if no external force acts on it.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Internal forces cannot change the total momentum of a system.
question_patterns: find the recoil velocity of a gun
calculate the final velocity after a collision
what is the total momentum of the system
determine the mass of an object using momentum conservation

solution_steps.explain: Sum the momenta of all parts before the interaction.
Total momentum is conserved, so p_final = p_initial.

concepts.title: Static Friction
concepts.definition: The resistive force that opposes the start of relative motion between two surfaces touching.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Static friction is self-adjusting up to a maximum limiting value.
question_patterns: calculate the maximum static frictional force
find the coefficient of static friction
what is the limiting friction
determine if a block will slide given an applied force

solution_steps.explain: On a level surface, normal force equals weight.
Limiting friction is the product of coefficient and normal force.

concepts.title: Kinetic Friction
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the frictional force acting between surfaces that are in relative motion.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Kinetic friction is indeed generally less than the maximum static friction.
question_patterns: calculate the kinetic frictional force
find the acceleration of a sliding block
what is the resistive force during motion
determine the coefficient of kinetic friction

solution_steps.explain: Normal force is mass times gravity on a level plane.
Kinetic friction is coefficient times normal force.

concepts.title: Centripetal Force
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the center-directed force required to maintain an object's uniform circular motion.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Centripetal force is not a new type of force but a requirement for circular paths.
question_patterns: calculate the centripetal force on a car
find the tension in a whirling string
what force keeps a planet in orbit
determine the force needed for a turn of radius r

solution_steps.explain: Force is mass times velocity squared divided by radius.

concepts.title: Max Speed on Level Road
concepts.definition: The maximum velocity a vehicle can achieve on a flat circular track without skidding.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Friction provides the necessary centripetal force on a level road.
question_patterns: find the maximum speed of a car on a turn
will the cyclist slip at this speed
calculate the safe speed for a radius r
what is the limit of velocity on a flat road

solution_steps.action: calculate product of mu, r, and g
solution_steps.explain: The square of max velocity depends on friction, radius, and gravity.
The maximum speed is the square root of the product.

Impulse is mass times change in velocity.
